raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The chat endpoint checks each tool's `parameters` against the JSON Schema 2020-12 metaschema on every request, on the API server's event loop. `Draft202012Validator.check_schema` is pure Python and takes about 0.7 ms per tool, so an agent that sends 18 tools adds 12 ms of blocking CPU to each request.

#42213 adds a cache and skips the check for schemas it has already seen. This PR instead makes the check itself about as fast as a cache read, so a new schema is fast too and no cache is needed.

## Modifications

- Check tool parameters with a `jsonschema_rs.Draft202012Validator` built once at import.
- Check `pattern` regexes and `$ref`/`$id`/`$schema` URIs with `check_schema`'s Python format checker.
- Add `jsonschema-rs==0.58.6` (MIT, prebuilt wheels) to every `pyproject`.
- Error messages keep the same form: the failing value, the keyword, and the location in the schema.

## Accuracy Tests

Model inputs and sampling are unchanged. On 41,559 schemas (edge cases, two fuzzers over real agent tool schemas, and nesting up to the HTTP body limit), the new check accepts and rejects the same schemas as `check_schema`, except schemas nested past Python's recursion limit (about 98 levels), which it accepts.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Checking the 18 tool schemas of a coding agent, median of 5,000 runs on one thread:

| | check_schema | jsonschema-rs |
|---|---|---|
| 18 tools | 12.6 ms | 0.06 ms |

End-to-end: Qwen3-8B on one H100, streamed chat with a cached 11K-token prefix (system prompt and the 18 tools) and 32 output tokens. One server ran both checks, alternating in blocks over 10 rounds per concurrency.

| Concurrency | TTFT p50 before (ms) | TTFT p50 after (ms) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 58.4 | 34.9 | −40% |
| 4 | 90.8 | 59.8 | −34% |
| 16 | 436.4 | 87.2 | −80% |

Unit tests pass, with one new test in `test_serving_chat.py`:
- `test_serving_chat.py` (151)
- `test_normalize_json_schema_types.py` (23)
- `test_json_schema_constraint.py` (18)

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body: i think this drops the formatting checks `check_schema` previously ran, so something like "[" can now pass kimi's non-strict auto path where no xgrammar validation runs, should we preserve those checks?
added them so we match `check_schema` (+ a test to catch this) and reran the CPU benchmark

This works and your speedup holds up. Only one of this and #46818 should land. As I measured it, this matches #46818 on repeated tools, and on first-seen schemas it saves about 40 ms of TTFT at 18 tools and about 230 ms at 81, where #46818 saves nothing. #46818 adds no dependency and keeps the same validator. I closed #42213, which cached the same check.

PPU CI needs a small fix before merge (inline on the import). The other inline comment is minor.

I tested d4bd420f77 merged on main e152f531d9 (582168dd7c for the nesting band), against that same main, on B200 with Python 3.12 and synthetic tool sets, since your 18-tool set isn't published.

Check time in ms for the whole tool set, median, on one core. First-seen means a new title, descriptions and `pattern` regexes each round.

| Tool set | `check_schema` | This PR, repeat | This PR, first-seen | #46818 hit | #46818 miss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 18 tools, 29.2 KB | 39.6 | 0.16 | 0.76 | 0.088 | 41.7 |
| 81 tools, 170.5 KB | 237 | 0.99 | 6.1 | 0.64 | 252 |

Your 0.06 ms holds up in scale: I measured about 5.5 us per KB, and your 12.6 ms for `check_schema` suggests about 9 KB, so about 0.05 ms. First-seen costs more because each new pattern goes through Python `re.compile`, and it's still about 50x faster than `check_schema` at 18 tools and about 40x at 81.

Median TTFT in ms over 3 alternating rounds, where c is concurrency. This is Llama-3.2-1B on one B200 per server, streaming, with `max_tokens` 1 and a cached prefix of about 10.6K tokens at 18 tools and 59.3K at 81. This CI model has no cookbook page, so it shows overhead only.

| Case | main | This PR | #46818 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18 tools, repeat, c=1 | 55.2 | 14.7 | 14.9 |
| 18 tools, repeat, c=8 | 378 | 51.5 | 51.5 |
| 18 tools, repeat, c=16 | 746 | 94.3 | 92.8 |
| 18 tools, first-seen, c=1 | 94.1 | 55.0 | 93.9 |
| 18 tools, first-seen, c=8 | 454 | 239 | 512 |
| 81 tools, repeat, c=1 | 278 | 38.5 | 38.8 |
| 81 tools, repeat, c=8 | 2102 | 173 | 180 |
| 81 tools, repeat, c=16 | 4189 | 371 | 355 |
| 81 tools, first-seen, c=1 | 989 | 763 | 1005 |
| 81 tools, first-seen, c=8 | 5333 | 3393 | 5330 |

At 18 tools and c=1 the saving matches the check cost (about 40 ms). Your Qwen3-8B saving (23.5 ms) is about 2x your 12.6 ms, and I didn't reproduce or explain that.

I fuzzed this against `check_schema` and probed real main and PR servers over HTTP. Beyond the deep nesting you documented, the only HTTP difference I found is that this PR rejects a trailing newline in `$anchor`, `$dynamicAnchor`, `$recursiveAnchor` or `$id`. On the gRPC bridge it also rejects NaN or Infinity in `maximum` or `minimum` and lone surrogates in keys or `pattern`. Invalid schemas still return 400 with the same prefix, and the text after the prefix changes.

On the default 8 MB stack the validator never overflowed at any depth `json.loads` can deliver. On smaller stacks it segfaults where main raises `RecursionError` (5,000 levels at 2 MB, 1,500 at 1 MB). orjson caps HTTP near 1,024 levels, but the bridge has no cap. I found nothing in the repo that shrinks the stack, so I'm only noting it.

Packaging looks fine. 0.58.6 is MIT with no runtime dependencies, and has abi3 wheels for manylinux x86_64, i686 and aarch64, musllinux x86_64 and aarch64, macOS and Windows, plus an sdist. There are no ppc64le, riscv64 or s390x wheels. The aarch64 glibc 2.28 floor isn't new, since the latest tiktoken and llguidance wheels are already at 2.28 and 2.31. It adds 14 MB on disk, 11.6 ms of import and 7.8 MB of RSS.

The chat validation, schema normalization, gRPC bridge and tool-calling server tests found no regressions on the merged tree.

Not checked: a live gRPC client (bridge results come from calling `_validate_request` directly), running anywhere but Linux x86_64 on Python 3.12 (other platforms got wheel listings or `pip download` only), multiple API or tokenizer workers, your Qwen3-8B setup and schema corpus, and the security history of jsonschema-rs or versions after 0.58.6. For #46818 I only measured timing and read the diff.

PPU sanity will probably fail at server launch on the merge push to main. This import runs when `http_server` loads, and that job won't have the package. `scripts/ci/ppu/build_and_test.sh` installs the built wheels with `--no-deps --no-index`, then adds only what `PINNED_ADDITIONS` lists. The package snapshot from main run 41340956934 (2026-11-01) has no jsonschema-rs on either runner, and without it the import fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jsonschema_rs'`. This PR doesn't run that job without the `run-ci-ppu` label, so nothing shows it here.

These files are on main but not on your branch yet, so merge main first. Then add `"jsonschema-rs": "0.58.6"` to `PINNED_ADDITIONS` in `scripts/ci/ppu/check_dependencies.py`, and update `ADDITIONS`, `WHEELS` and the expected output of `test_requirements_cli_emits_only_pinned_evaluators` in `test_ppu_ci_dependencies.py`. The wheel-name regex accepts the abi3 wheel. I traced this and ran nothing on PPU hardware, and I didn't run that test with all three fixtures updated.

nodes.body:
Minor: schemas that main rejects with a 400 for being too deep can now get a 500. On Llama-3.2-1B, `properties` nesting returns 200 up to 480 levels, then `Internal server error: maximum recursion depth exceeded` at about 495 to 508, from `tojson` in the chat template. From 510 levels orjson returns 400. `anyOf` at 500 and `dependencies` at 1000 also return 500. The server stays up, and main already returns this 500 for `default` or `x-meta` nested 1000 levels. The description covers the new acceptance but not this 500.

Adding `RecursionError` to `_CHAT_TEMPLATE_CLIENT_ERRORS` fixes both. On the merged tree, those cases then returned 400 with `maximum recursion depth exceeded`, while valid schemas, `properties` 450, `anyOf` 450, `items` 900 and `x-meta` 800 stayed 200. I only tried the Llama 3.2 template, so the band may differ on others.
